subject: history
title: Hitler's Seizure of Power
welcome_lead: From the chancellorship of 30 January to the Enabling Act of 23 March 1933.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on Hitler's appointment and the consolidation of power in 1933.
final_note: You have witnessed democracy dismantled in 53 days.

concepts.def: Hitler appointed Chancellor of Germany by President Hindenburg on 30 January 1933.
Fire on 27 February 1933 blamed on Marinus van der Lubbe and used to justify emergency decree.
Issued 28 February 1933 suspending civil liberties under Article 48.
Law of 23 March 1933 (Gesetz zur Behebung der Not) granting Hitler power to legislate without parliament.
'Coordination' of German society, abolishing trade unions on 2 May and other parties by July 1933.
Agreement of 20 July 1933 between the Vatican and Nazi Germany guaranteeing Catholic rights in return for political withdrawal.

walkthroughs.body_html: The July 1932 election gave the NSDAP 37.3 per cent and 230 seats, making it the largest party but lacking a majority. The November 1932 election saw Nazi support fall to 33 per cent. Backstairs intrigue by Papen and Schleicher led Hindenburg to appoint Hitler with only three Nazis in cabinet, hoping to constrain him. The miscalculation proved fatal to Weimar democracy.

walkthroughs.h2: From Reichstag Fire to Enabling Act
walkthroughs.body_html: The Reichstag Fire on 27 February allowed the Reichstag Fire Decree of 28 February to suspend civil liberties. The 5 March election produced 43.9 per cent Nazi support. After arresting Communist deputies and securing Centre Party support, the Enabling Act passed on 23 March with 444 votes to 94 (SPD voting against). The Act provided legal cover for dictatorial rule until 1937.

Trade unions were abolished on 2 May and replaced by the DAF. The 14 July Law against the Formation of New Parties made the NSDAP the only legal party. The Concordat with the Vatican (20 July) brought international legitimacy. State governments were brought under direct Reich control by April. Civil service was purged of Jews and political opponents from 7 April.
